judgment.notes: No E/M applications occur. Cauchy–Schwarz is applied to finitely supported real shell sequences, translated reflections, and finite sequences of shell norms; reflection/translation preserves counting measure and restricting a sequence cannot increase its ell2 norm. The geometric ratio is 2^(-1/2), strictly between zero and one. BG001–BG003 give the routine facts and actual grounds.

For each ordering (relabeling slots accordingly), zero sum gives 2^j1 <= largest magnitude <= three times the second-largest magnitude < 6*2^j2, hence j1-j2 <= 2. Each shell has 2^(j+1) elements. The displayed convolution bound follows by fixing the two smaller frequencies and applying Cauchy–Schwarz to the larger pair, then to the smaller shell sums. N3 >= 2^j3 leaves the displayed 2^(-(j3-j4)/2) weight. Dropping j3 <= j2 factors the nonnegative sum; the shifted shell-norm products and geometric offset sum give the product of the four norms. At most 24 orderings and three offsets give an absolute constant. Exhausting frequencies by |k| <= m and then taking the supremum proves the infinite claim; subset monotonicity proves the last clause.
